physical_subject: How can hinged rods copy an outline at twice the size?
relationship: Similar triangles in an ideal pantograph keep the tracing and copying points on a common ray at a fixed distance ratio.
operation: A fixed-ratio parallelogram linkage traces a leaf-like outline at two scales, with matching triangles exposed.
closest_prior: objects/03-shadow and context/02-camera: similar-triangle optical measurements; old matrix/grid introductions
substantive_difference: A constrained parallelogram copying instrument maintains homothety during arbitrary reachable planar tracing; the geometric invariant is built into rigid rods.
